chunks: Abān ibn Taghlib narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Daughters are good deeds, and sons are a blessing. Good deeds are rewarded for, and a blessing is questioned about.

key_terms.الْبَنَاتُ: daughters; female children regarded here as a source of spiritual reward
key_terms.الْبَنُونَ: sons; male children described here as a blessing
key_terms.حَسَنَاتٌ: good deeds; acts or means through which reward is granted
key_terms.نِعْمَةٌ: a blessing; a favor granted by Allah for which one is accountable
key_terms.يُسْأَلُ: is questioned; is subject to accountability

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describe daughters and sons in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a moral perspective on children, portraying daughters as a source of reward and sons as a divine blessing. It encourages gratitude, proper valuation of daughters, and awareness that blessings from Allah are a trust for which one will be questioned.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4692 - Aban ibn Taghlib narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) who said: "
Daughters are good deeds, and sons are blessings. Good deeds are rewarded, and blessings are questioned about."
